classification.difficultyReason: Factor the numerator, distinguish the two signs of x-1 in the absolute-value denominator, preserve the excluded input after cancellation, and sketch two restricted lines with distinct open endpoints.

content.prompt: Simplify $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-1}{|x-1|}$ and hence sketch the graph of $y=f(x)$.

answer.short:
$f(x)=\begin{cases}x+1,&x>1,\\-x-1,&x<1.\end{cases}$

The function is undefined at $x=1$. The graph has open endpoints at $(1,2)$ and $(1,-2)$.
answer.worked:
The denominator is zero at $x=1$, so this value is excluded.

For $x>1$,
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-1}\\f(x)&=x+1.\end{align*}$$
For $x<1$,
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{-(x-1)}\\f(x)&=-x-1.\end{align*}$$
Sketch the two restricted straight lines, leaving both endpoints at $x=1$ open.

spec.description: Corrected graph: two disconnected rays with open endpoints at x=1. The erroneous continuous V in the answer book is not reproduced.
spec.mathematics: y=-x-1 for x<1 and y=x+1 for x>1; no value at x=1.
